## Decisions

- `kb:adr/process-land-skill-is-the-landing-ritual` — Landing is its own step: it gates on an approved review, composes the closing subject, shows the predicted bump, pushes, and deletes the branch by content diff. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: release, triage) → `docs/adr/process-land-skill-is-the-landing-ritual.md`
- `kb:adr/process-release-breaking-marker-bang-gated` — The exclamation mark is the only breaking marker, legal only when a human sets MUSTER_BREAKING=1; the footer phrase is banned outright by the hook. (accepted, 2026-09-01; features: release) → `docs/adr/process-release-breaking-marker-bang-gated.md`
- `kb:adr/process-release-bump-map-widened-perf-refactor` — A feat bumps minor; fix, perf and refactor bump patch; every other type releases nothing. svu hardwires only feat and fix, so the workflow shims the other two. (accepted, 2026-09-01; features: release) → `docs/adr/process-release-bump-map-widened-perf-refactor.md`
- `kb:adr/process-release-commitlint-eleven-types` — Commit types are the eleven-strong commitlint conventional list, plus review(<plan>) on plan branches only; the list is enforced by a commit-msg hook. (accepted, 2026-09-01; features: release) → `docs/adr/process-release-commitlint-eleven-types.md`
- `kb:adr/process-release-notes-derived-from-bumping-types` — Release notes are derived: the changelog filter includes exactly the four bumping types, whose subjects publish verbatim and are capped at 72 characters. (accepted, 2026-09-01; features: release) → `docs/adr/process-release-notes-derived-from-bumping-types.md`
- `kb:adr/process-release-v0-clamp-v1-deliberate` — The release workflow runs svu with the v0 clamp, so no marker cuts 1.0.0 by accident; version 1 is cut by deliberately removing the flag. (accepted, 2026-09-01; features: release) → `docs/adr/process-release-v0-clamp-v1-deliberate.md`
- `kb:adr/release-builds-cross-compiled-on-linux` — Release builds run on a Linux runner and cross-compile darwin with cgo disabled, which every dependency permits; a standing reason not to add cgo casually. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: release) → `docs/adr/release-builds-cross-compiled-on-linux.md`
- `kb:adr/release-distribution-github-release-not-brew` — Distribution is the tagged GitHub Release: an install target downloads the latest darwin archive; Homebrew is deferred to any open-sourcing. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: release) → `docs/adr/release-distribution-github-release-not-brew.md`
- `kb:adr/release-drops-js-sourcemap` — Release builds omit the dashboard's JavaScript sourcemap; local and E2E builds keep it, so the shipped artifact differs from the tested one by the maps alone. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: release, connection) → `docs/adr/release-drops-js-sourcemap.md`
- `kb:adr/release-two-arch-archives-not-universal` — The release ships separate amd64 and arm64 darwin archives rather than a universal binary; the installer picks by machine architecture. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: release) → `docs/adr/release-two-arch-archives-not-universal.md`
- `kb:adr/triage-issue-closes-when-fix-lands` — An issue closes when the fix lands on main via a closes reference in the squash subject, never at triage; duplicates and invalid issues close with approval. (accepted, 2026-08-31; features: triage, release) → `docs/adr/triage-issue-closes-when-fix-lands.md`

## Retired, rejected and superseded

- `kb:adr/release-no-ci-test-job-yet` — No test or lint job runs in CI for now; the release build is the compile gate, and adding the check target is one step when open-sourcing makes it worth having. (rejected, 2026-08-31; features: release) → `docs/adr/release-no-ci-test-job-yet.md`
- `kb:adr/release-versioning-automatic-from-conventional-commits` — Versions are computed from conventional commits since the last tag on every push to main; Muster stays on 0.x, so the breaking marker is not used. (superseded, 2026-08-31; features: release) → `docs/adr/release-versioning-automatic-from-conventional-commits.md`
